title: Cities Skylines | Franklin, Episode 1: Prehistory
premise: Donoteat rejects Cities: Skylines’ frictionless mayor-as-god model, introduces historical time through floodplain formation, and builds Lenape settlements as Franklin’s precolonial foundation, with caveats about their accuracy.
coverage: The instant-city opening gives way to river formation, Lenape settlement building and a closing urban-policy montage. The presenter acknowledges inaccuracies in his depiction of Lenape agriculture and village layouts. Historical claims and place-name translations are his account.

panels.heading: False start: standard city series
panels.description: Cities: Skylines main menu and map-selection interface begin the deliberately conventional opening.
panels.camera: Static menu screens, followed by map selection and loading.
panels.action: A map is selected; nothing happens in the game world yet.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the satire of inherited infrastructure and instant cities.

panels.heading: The blank square
panels.description: An empty square of grass and trees is divided by a steep river, with highway stubs at its edges.
panels.camera: Overhead view of the whole map, then a closer look at the highway.
panels.action: The landscape loads with no settlement on it.
panels.visualGag: Sets up the ready-made highway joke and the later rejection of a blank-slate city.

panels.heading: Someone thought ahead
panels.description: Two paired highway stubs terminate beside a dashed tile boundary.
panels.camera: The view tightens over the highway stubs.
panels.action: No roads are being built here.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the joke about supplied connections: the infrastructure arrives before any people or history.

panels.heading: Beautiful waterfront, inconvenient ravine
panels.description: A deep, steep-banked river fills the editor view while the road toolbar is open.
panels.camera: Closer overhead view of the river.
panels.action: The road tools open.
panels.visualGag: Setup: the supposedly desirable waterfront needs an absurd instant bridge.

panels.heading: Giant bridge in seconds
panels.description: A long elevated bridge spans the water on substantial piers.
panels.camera: A blue placement preview gives way to the finished bridge, seen from a new oblique angle.
panels.action: The bridge preview becomes a placed road, with no construction workers in sight.
panels.visualGag: Payoff: the finished bridge appears almost at once, which makes the missing engineering constraints literal.

panels.heading: Zoning without mixed use
panels.description: Green residential zoning occupies two rectangular blocks beside a road grid.
panels.camera: Overhead editor view as the road grid goes down and the zoning cells fill in.
panels.action: Roads and residential zones are placed.
panels.visualGag: The instant-city satire continues, with a menu grid standing in for the negotiation behind mixed-use streets.

panels.heading: Water without environmental law
panels.description: White water-info overlay shows blue river water, intake/outlet placement and tool icons.
panels.camera: A utility overlay replaces the normal terrain colors.
panels.action: Water facilities are selected and placed.
panels.visualGag: The overlay goes with the narration's effortless shortcuts: pure water that needs no treatment and sewage dumped in the river.

panels.heading: Pipes without gravity
panels.description: Water-pipe network forms loops beneath the neighborhood in the white/blue utility view.
panels.camera: Overhead utility view as the network grows.
panels.action: Pipes are drawn through the terrain.
panels.visualGag: The pipes illustrate the spoken joke about ignoring gravity and tunneling; the game shows no digging.

panels.heading: The tiny coal plant
panels.description: A compact roadside power plant sits beside otherwise largely empty grass.
panels.camera: Close oblique view after placement in the power overlay, then back to the info coloring.
panels.action: The plant is placed from the toolbar.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the “world’s tiniest” infrastructure motif: the plant looks absurdly small.

panels.heading: A municipality as a toolbar
panels.description: Service placement view shows small buildings with satisfaction icons alongside a regular road grid.
panels.camera: Utility, health and fire overlays follow one another while the camera stays put.
panels.action: A landfill, health services and fire services are placed in turn.
panels.visualGag: Continues the frictionless-institution gag that started with the power plant.

panels.heading: People actually live here
panels.description: A detached-house information window appears over the newly occupied subdivision.
panels.camera: Alternates between a close look at the house and a wider view of the neighborhood.
panels.action: A house is selected, with homes lining the grid.
panels.visualGag: Sets up the park displacement gag by showing that the parcel is occupied.

panels.heading: The benevolent park
panels.description: Purple park-placement area overlays occupied houses in leisure view and smiley icons appear.
panels.camera: Placement preview, then back to normal coloring.
panels.action: The park is placed, and the game responds with happy icons.
panels.visualGag: The cheerful indicators come first; concern about the lost housing follows.

panels.heading: What happened to the house?
panels.description: Normal neighborhood view shows the new park amid detached houses.
panels.camera: The same neighborhood; a bulldozer tool appears shortly afterward.
panels.action: An occupied building has given way to the park. Which household lived there is not shown.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the park setup: the game's positive feedback ignores the narrator's questions about the displaced residents and their compensation.

panels.heading: Ban pets instead
panels.description: City Policies menu and explanatory tooltips cover the pale neighborhood view.
panels.camera: The policy menu opens over the view; the camera stays put.
panels.action: Policy options are browsed.
panels.visualGag: The displacement joke continues: banning pets and other abstract policies are absurd answers to losing a home.

panels.heading: Money from nowhere
panels.description: Economy window covers a night-lit miniature neighborhood.
panels.camera: The Economy window opens over the same night scene.
panels.action: The budget and tax menu opens.
panels.visualGag: The opaque income and tax screen finishes the institutional satire without ever answering the compensation question.

panels.heading: Reject the god mayor
panels.description: Night subdivision remains on screen after the financial window closes.
panels.camera: Oblique game view, then a cut to lettering on black.
panels.action: The menus close; no residents react.
panels.visualGag: End of the opening satire: the instant town is dropped as the model for Franklin.

panels.heading: For the first time on YouTube
panels.description: White “FOR THE FIRST TIME ON YOUTUBE” text on black.
panels.camera: Static title card, then black.
panels.action: Title text only.
panels.visualGag: The grand premiere framing contrasts with the glib conventional build that came before.

panels.heading: Franklin revealed
panels.description: Gold FRANKLIN and Liberty Bell above “A DONOTEAT [round emblem] SERIES” on black.
panels.camera: Static title graphic, followed by a transition through black and the emblem.
panels.action: The title elements appear; no characters.

panels.heading: Messy history, not a god
panels.description: EPISODE 1 / PREHISTORY banner accompanies huts arranged beside a dirt path.
panels.camera: The view moves from the river edge to the hut settlement.
panels.action: Huts, fence/rack props and fire are placed around the path.

panels.heading: Introduce hydrology
panels.description: HYDROLOGY and its definition overlay an overhead river-and-forest view.
panels.camera: Wider terrain view than the village shots, with static explanatory text.
panels.action: Terrain tools open; no characters.

panels.heading: The game’s deep channel
panels.description: Tan/blue cross-section graphic depicts a deep narrow river trough over gameplay.
panels.camera: Static diagram over the editor, whose framing shifts behind it.
panels.action: The diagram illustrates the narration while the terrain cursor stays visible.

panels.heading: Canyon exception
panels.description: Photograph of a blue river inside rocky canyon walls fills much of the screen.
panels.camera: A static photo inset, then back to gameplay.
panels.action: No characters.

panels.heading: Shallow channel and floodplains
panels.description: A broad shallow cross-section labelled SHALLOW CHANNEL overlays the hut/river editor view.
panels.camera: A new static diagram, much shallower than the earlier steep channel.
panels.action: The terrain brush reshapes the riverbank behind the diagram.

panels.heading: Floodwater spreads
panels.description: Broad blue water shape in cross-section extends onto shallow side margins.
panels.camera: Static diagram over shifting overhead views of the terrain.
panels.action: The brush works along the river while the diagram shows the overflow.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the sediment inserts: the sober floodplain explanation is about to be interrupted by dirt and poop.

panels.heading: Very slowly
panels.description: VERY SLOWLY labels both shallow margins of the blue floodwater diagram.
panels.camera: Static text and diagram.
panels.action: The labels explain the slow flow at the margins; no people.
panels.visualGag: Part of the sediment-list setup: the slow floodwater carries the material shown next.

panels.heading: Dirt insert
panels.description: Close image of muddy material replaces the diagram briefly.
panels.camera: Quick cut to a static close-up.
panels.action: No characters.
panels.visualGag: First item in the dirt-to-poop escalation, just before the emoji.

panels.heading: Poop emoji payoff
panels.description: Giant smiling poop emoji covers the river editor view.
panels.camera: Static poop emoji over the gameplay, followed by a gravestone and then the diagram again.
panels.action: Terrain editor continues beneath the cartoon.
panels.visualGag: The cartoon bodily payoff in the dirt, poop and dead-bodies escalation; the gravestone that follows completes the list.

panels.heading: Dead bodies: gravestone payoff
panels.description: Photograph of a weathered rounded gravestone in a grassy cemetery overlays the terrain editor.
panels.camera: Static gravestone photograph after the poop emoji.
panels.action: No characters.
panels.visualGag: Completes the escalation: a cemetery marker stands in for the morbid last item, dead bodies, right after the smiling poop emoji. The cement-shoes line continues as spoken crime humor.
panels.notes: No corpse is shown, and the inscription can't be made out.

panels.heading: Return to sedimentation
panels.description: Broad shallow cutaway overlays the wider river landscape again.
panels.camera: The diagram returns over changing editor views.
panels.action: Terrain brush alters the river edges.
panels.visualGag: Back to the sober explanation after the dirt, poop emoji and gravestone. Only the dead bodies get a picture; the cement shoes stay spoken.

panels.heading: Flat land takes time
panels.description: High overhead view shows broad flattened river areas with narrower tributaries.
panels.camera: Moves from close terrain to a broad overhead view, then down to a low riverbank view.
panels.action: Terrain grading continues; nothing is built.

panels.heading: Rome comparison
panels.description: Sepia reconstruction of monumental Rome is vertically inserted over the river editor.
panels.camera: Static illustration inset; the recording interface flashes up briefly later.
panels.action: The drawing stays still.
panels.visualGag: Setup for the flood-disaster illustration that follows: the Rome comparison leads to the dark, literal payoff that everyone has a flooding problem.

panels.heading: You are not special
panels.description: Historical flood-catastrophe illustration overlays gameplay: torrential brown water carries wrecked houses and debris against a stone-arched bridge; burning debris and people struggling in the water compound the disaster.
panels.camera: Cut to a static painting, with some gameplay between it and the Rome image.
panels.action: The figures are part of a still artwork.
panels.visualGag: The catastrophic flood picture gives 'Everyone has a problem with flooding' a dark, literal payoff.
panels.notes: The artwork may be Kurz & Allison’s 1889 Johnstown Flood lithograph.

panels.heading: Fishing settlement shore
panels.description: Dirt path reaches a sandy riverbank; canoe/hut props are being added.
panels.camera: Approaches the shore from a higher view.
panels.action: Beach and canoes are placed.

panels.heading: Lenape regional extent
panels.description: Green regional map labelled Lenni Lenape covers the editor view.
panels.camera: Static map inset, then back to gameplay.
panels.action: No characters.

panels.heading: Correct the subsistence portrayal
panels.description: Rounded huts flank the path toward the canoe beach.
panels.camera: Oblique overhead view moving between the beach and the path.
panels.action: The hut scene is edited; no farming is shown.
panels.visualGag: The self-correction is spoken: he says this depiction makes the culture look too primitive.

panels.heading: Build the wilderness appearance
panels.description: Many trees now surround the huts and path to the shore.
panels.camera: Changes scale and angle around the same settlement.
panels.action: Trees are selected, duplicated and placed.

panels.heading: Detail the fishing village
panels.description: Canoes line the beach beside huts; small props and a fire enrich the central clearing.
panels.camera: Moves in and out around the shore and the inland village.
panels.action: Vegetation and shore props are added in the editor.

panels.heading: Prepare another riverbank
panels.description: Terrain tools and contours appear beside a broad river bend.
panels.camera: Overhead and oblique views as the grading progresses.
panels.action: River edge is flattened and textured.

panels.heading: Duplicate a new row of huts
panels.description: Huts line a dirt path with dense tree cover behind them.
panels.camera: From selecting huts to a wider wooded view.
panels.action: Huts and tree groups are duplicated along the path.

panels.heading: Prepare the main village
panels.description: Fresh flat bank and water edge fill the editor while terrain tools remain open.
panels.camera: From grading the bank to laying out a curved dirt path.
panels.action: The site is leveled and a path drawn.

panels.heading: Fortified-village reference
panels.description: Drawing of an oval palisade village shows houses around a central gathering/fire area.
panels.camera: Static reference drawing, then back to the editor.
panels.action: The figures in the drawing are static. He says outright that he can't vouch for the layout's historical accuracy.

panels.heading: Lay out the huts
panels.description: Rounded huts gather around a curved dirt path, before walls enclose them.
panels.camera: More huts appear around the same curved path.
panels.action: Huts are selected and placed; the recording overlay briefly cuts in.

panels.heading: Build the palisade
panels.description: Tall stake wall forms a large oval around the huts.
panels.camera: The wall grows while the camera moves in toward the perimeter.
panels.action: Palisade segments are placed and ground texture adjusted.

panels.heading: Growth outside the walls
panels.description: Huts extend beyond the palisade along an outer dirt path.
panels.camera: Moves across the rows inside and outside the walls.
panels.action: More huts are placed outside the enclosure.

panels.heading: Drying racks and daily-life props
panels.description: White fence/rack forms surround huts and fires inside and outside the wall.
panels.camera: Alternates between the wider layout and a tighter interior view.
panels.action: Rack, fence and small pile props are added; nobody uses them.

panels.heading: Canoes finish the main village
panels.description: Wide oblique view shows palisade village beside water with canoes along shore.
panels.camera: A close view of the shore placement, then a wider view.
panels.action: Canoes and shore detailing complete the complex.

panels.heading: Surround the village with forest
panels.description: Dense trees border the completed palisade and its approach path.
panels.camera: Moves around the site and pulls out to a regional view.
panels.action: Large tree selections are duplicated and placed.

panels.heading: Build another small village
panels.description: A line of huts beside a dirt path and campfire gains shoreline canoes and trees.
panels.camera: From a short dirt path to a wooded shore village.
panels.action: Huts, fire, canoes and tree assets are added.

panels.heading: Terrain-theme change
panels.description: Riverbank and hillside now have a craggy rocky texture with scattered conifers.
panels.camera: Shoreline views showing the new terrain look.
panels.action: Vegetation editing continues; the theme switch itself isn't shown.

panels.heading: A city through the present
panels.description: Low oblique view of a bright campfire, huts, canoes and river precedes closing-agenda inserts.
panels.camera: Low close view after the high editor framing.
panels.action: Settlement props sit by the fire; no villagers appear.
panels.visualGag: Sets up the rapid agenda montage, which pairs serious topics with comic inserts.

panels.heading: Eminent domain
panels.description: Photograph shows a house stranded amid new paved road lanes.
panels.camera: Static inset over the terrain editor.
panels.action: No characters.
panels.visualGag: A pointed payoff to the opening displacement gag: the house stuck in the road shows property interests colliding.

panels.heading: Zoning
panels.description: Colored zoning diagram with category legend overlays forest/editor grid.
panels.camera: Static diagram, just before the police insert.
panels.action: No characters.

panels.heading: The police: airborne cruiser
panels.description: Police cruiser is pictured airborne above a street, with the visible caption '(siren blaring)'.
panels.camera: Cut to a still of the airborne cruiser.
panels.action: The car is frozen mid-jump.
panels.visualGag: The airborne police car turns the sober police-policy item into a movie stunt.
panels.notes: The film or television source of the police car is unidentified, and it is unknown whether an actual siren plays.

panels.heading: Not in my backyard
panels.description: Cartoon protest contains NOT IN MY BACKYARD lettering and a WIND POWER opposition sign.
panels.camera: Static cartoon inset.
panels.action: The drawn figures stay still.
panels.visualGag: The exaggerated, hostile protesters caricature the NIMBYism and YIMBYism item.

panels.heading: Public housing
panels.description: Black-and-white aerial depicts a complex of tall slab buildings.
panels.camera: Static photograph.
panels.action: No characters.

panels.heading: Highways
panels.description: Dense vehicle-filled circular/curving road and parking formation fills the insert.
panels.camera: Static aerial photograph.
panels.action: Still image; nothing moves.

panels.heading: Redlining
panels.description: Colored city map divides areas into red, yellow, green and blue categories.
panels.camera: Static map inset over the gameplay.
panels.action: No characters.

panels.heading: Railroads and transit
panels.description: Thomas the Tank Engine from Thomas & Friends, a smiling blue locomotive, is pictured on tracks.
panels.camera: Cut to a static children's-cartoon image.
panels.action: Still image.
panels.visualGag: Thomas the Tank Engine is an incongruous children's-TV illustration for the serious transit item.

panels.heading: Speculative development
panels.description: Oblique aerial shows tightly packed city blocks and distant skyline.
panels.camera: Static photo replacing the Thomas image.
panels.action: No characters.

panels.heading: Political machines
panels.description: The Simpsons radio-studio still shows KBBL hosts Bill and Marty at a desk beside broadcasting equipment.
panels.camera: Static Simpsons still.
panels.action: Still image.
panels.visualGag: The Simpsons still of Bill and Marty goes with political machines. Which episode or pun it points to is unclear.

panels.heading: Eds and meds: debt mountain
panels.description: Mountain illustration bears the large word DEBT.
panels.camera: Static inset replacing the Simpsons still.
panels.action: No characters.
panels.visualGag: The literal mountain of debt turns the institutional-finance item into a visual metaphor.

panels.heading: Essential services: provision
panels.description: Workers stand in an excavated trench around a large pipe.
panels.camera: Static worksite photograph.
panels.action: The workers are posed in a still photo.
panels.visualGag: Sets up the contrast between clean public service and the dirty water of privatization.

panels.heading: Privatized services: dirty tap
panels.description: Orange-brown water flows from a tap into a white sink in the inserted photograph.
panels.camera: Static photograph.
panels.action: No characters.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the service gag: working municipal infrastructure gives way to visibly dirty tap water for the privatization item. No particular scandal is named.

panels.heading: Financialization
panels.description: Tall modern waterfront tower is inserted over the map editor.
panels.camera: Static photograph; the recording interface flashes up briefly.
panels.action: No characters.
panels.visualGag: Leads into the capitalist imagery of the class-divide insert. The tower is unidentified.

panels.heading: Racism
panels.description: Black-and-white photograph shows hooded Ku Klux Klan marchers along a street with the Capitol dome behind them.
panels.camera: Static historical photograph.
panels.action: The marchers are frozen in the still.
panels.notes: The photograph’s date and precise attribution are uncertain.

panels.heading: Class divides
panels.description: Monopoly mascot Rich Uncle Pennybags (Mr. Monopoly) carries a dollar-sign money sack, wearing his top hat.
panels.camera: Static black-and-white cartoon that stays on screen.
panels.action: The running pose is drawn, not animated.
panels.visualGag: Rich Uncle Pennybags is the literal board-game capitalist for class divides. He follows the separate Klan photograph for racism and continues from the financialization tower.

panels.heading: LGBTQ issues
panels.description: Stonewall Inn facade includes its sign and rainbow decoration.
panels.camera: Static photograph.
panels.action: No characters.

panels.heading: Historic preservation
panels.description: Modern box-shaped building stands immediately beside an older brick facade.
panels.camera: Static photo, followed by a browser view of an article version.
panels.action: No characters.
panels.visualGag: The pairing may contrast preservation with redevelopment; beyond the clash of styles, the point is unclear.

panels.heading: Everyone’s favorite parking
panels.description: Full-screen Houston aerial is dominated by parking areas and yellow Parkings title.
panels.camera: Static full-screen image.
panels.action: Nothing moves.
panels.visualGag: Payoff to the mundane final agenda item: vast parking coverage and “Are you quite sure this is what you want?” text satirize automobile-dominated urbanism.

panels.heading: Donation appeal and cinematic transition
panels.description: High overhead landscape view returns before the final city-information UI.
panels.camera: Back from the parking image, with a brief city-info window before the cinematics.
panels.action: The editor view sets up the transition; no characters.
panels.visualGag: The joke about recording hiss and equipment is spoken only; nothing on screen illustrates it.

panels.heading: Kingsessing: place of the meadows
panels.description: Named canoe beach with huts, central fire and dense forest. Caption reads Kingsessing / Place of the meadows.
panels.camera: The view angle changes across the beach, orbiting the settlement.
panels.action: The finished settlement is shown, with no people.

panels.heading: Nockamixon: three houses?
panels.description: Forest clearing of huts and drying-rack shapes bears Nockamixon / Where there are three houses.
panels.camera: Moves closer and around the clearing.
panels.action: The village assets sit still.
panels.visualGag: The caption says three houses, but more than three huts are visible. It is unclear whether that is a joke or just the inherited translation of the place name.

panels.heading: Passyunk: between the hills
panels.description: Huts encircle a dirt clearing and fire; caption reads Passyunk / Place between the hills.
panels.camera: Changes angle and approaches the clearing.
panels.action: No people.

panels.heading: Shackamaxon: council place
panels.description: Forest village with huts, fence/rack props and central fire is labelled Shackamaxon / Place of the council.
panels.camera: Moves around the same clearing, then cuts to another shoreline.
panels.action: No people.

panels.heading: Aramingo revealed
panels.description: Large palisade village, exterior huts and shore canoes are labelled Aramingo / Wolf walk.
panels.camera: Moves along the shoreline to reveal the walled complex.
panels.action: No people; props and flames are visible.

panels.heading: Inside and outside Aramingo
panels.description: View turns around palisade toward water, revealing hut rows and central fires.
panels.camera: Views from opposite sides of the palisade, as if circling it.
panels.action: The walls, huts and fires are on display.

panels.heading: Manayunk: where we go to drink
panels.description: Canoe beach village carries Manayunk / Place where we go to drink.
panels.camera: Reveals the shore through the trees, then circles the settlement.
panels.action: No people drinking and no alcohol on screen.
panels.visualGag: The wry translation may hint at a modern association with the place.

panels.heading: Moyamensing: pigeon droppings
panels.description: Canoe beach with huts and fire carries Moyamensing / Place of pigeon droppings.
panels.camera: Changes angle at the same shore.
panels.action: No pigeons, droppings or people are visible.
panels.visualGag: The unromantic translation sets up the ending gag, as the same label carries over a cut to a different settlement.

panels.heading: Still Moyamensing
panels.description: Inland oval village replaces the beach while Moyamensing / Place of pigeon droppings remains. Ground-path lettering reads Still Moyamensing.
panels.camera: Cut to a separate inland settlement, then several angles around it.
panels.action: Huts, rack props and a fire sit still.
panels.visualGag: The ending callback: the Moyamensing label stays put and the ground text insists Still Moyamensing, carrying the pigeon-droppings joke across two locations.

panels.heading: End on black
panels.description: Black final image; no separate credit card is visible.
panels.camera: Black after the last named village.
panels.action: Nothing on screen.
